title: Tortilla Espanola
subtitle: The thick Spanish potato omelette that needs nothing more than eggs and olive oil
excerpt: A classic Spanish potato omelette, slowly cooked in olive oil until the potatoes are tender, then set into a thick, golden disc.
sourceNotes: A foundational recipe of Spanish home cooking, made in every household across the country.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten at room temperature within a few hours of cooking. Keeps refrigerated for up to 2 days.

glossaryTerms.definition: In Spain, a thick potato and egg omelette cooked in olive oil, unrelated to Mexican flatbreads.

content.text: This tortilla serves 4 and takes 45 minutes from start to finish. It is one of the most satisfying things to cook: simple ingredients, very little equipment, and a result that works warm, at room temperature, or cold the next day.

Use a 26cm frying pan with a lid or a large plate to flip. The flip is the only technically demanding moment: use a plate wider than the pan, invert confidently with one swift motion, then slide the tortilla back in. Hesitation is what causes it to break.

Heat the olive oil in a 26cm frying pan over a medium-low heat. Add the potato slices and onion. They should be submerged or nearly submerged in the oil. Cook gently for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are completely tender but not coloured.
Drain the potato and onion through a colander set over a bowl, catching the oil. Leave to cool for 5 minutes.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl and season well with black pepper. Add the drained potato and onion and mix gently to combine. Leave to rest for 5 minutes so the eggs begin to absorb into the potato.

Return 2 tablespoons of the reserved oil to the pan and heat over a medium heat. Pour in the egg and potato mixture and spread evenly. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes until the edges are set and the centre still wobbles slightly.

Place a large flat plate over the pan. In one confident motion, flip the pan so the tortilla lands on the plate. Add another splash of oil to the pan, then slide the tortilla back in, uncooked side down. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes more until just set.
Slide onto a board and rest for 5 minutes before cutting into wedges. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.problem: The tortilla stuck to the pan during the flip
items.solution: Make sure the pan is well oiled before the second side goes in. A non-stick pan helps enormously here.

items.problem: The centre is still very runny after cooking both sides
items.solution: Cover the pan with a lid for the last 2 minutes. The trapped steam will gently finish setting the centre without overcooking the edges.

items.problem: The potatoes are still firm in the finished tortilla
items.solution: They need the full 20 minutes of gentle poaching in oil. Rushing this step on a higher heat colours them before they are cooked through.

content.text: This is one of the great simple dishes of Spanish cooking. A proper

is served in bars across Spain from breakfast through to a late supper. It travels well, making it suited to picnics and packed lunches. Some cooks prefer it slightly runny in the centre; others like it fully set. Both are correct. The only wrong tortilla is a dry, overcooked one.
